_about: Hand-labelled verdicts for the wild sweep — one entry per finding, keyed by
pinned sweep and scores it against this file.
tp  — what witness said about the diff is factually true AND worth a
fp  — the statement is false, or trivially not worth attention
This produces PRECISION. It cannot produce recall: knowing what witness
MISSED would mean labelling all 171 commits by hand, not just the 31 it
spoke about. Nothing here should be read as a claim about recall in the
wild — the corpus in corpus/cases.js measures recall, and it is synthetic.
Single rater, and the rater maintains the tool. That is a real weakness, and
a smaller one than the synthetic corpus, where the same person wrote the
cases AND the detector. Second opinions are welcome as pull requests against
this file; disagreements are the point. If you flip a verdict, say why in
`why` and leave the old reasoning in the commit message.

sweep.rules: scanner default (suppression and deleted check excluded)

Fixing this needs the detector to tell a rewritten test from a replaced one, which line proximity cannot do.
